title: Supervised Learning — The Label Is Not Always Truth
key_insight: Label noise means some recorded answers are wrong or uncertain. Clear instructions, repeated reviews, and agreement checks reveal how trustworthy labels are.
body:
## The Label Is Not Always Truth

Two reviewers disagree about whether a support message is angry. The label looks definite in the table, but it came from a human judgment.

Label noise means some recorded answers are wrong or uncertain. Clear instructions, repeated reviews, and agreement checks reveal how trustworthy labels are.

Also check who is missing from the data. A model can score well overall while failing a smaller group that received fewer or poorer labels.
common_mistakes: Treating training accuracy as proof that new cases will work.
Using a classification score for a numeric prediction problem.
Assuming every recorded label is perfectly correct.
mini_exercise: Draw the situation from “The Label Is Not Always Truth” with three labeled steps, then explain what changes at each step.
real_world_usage: Most practical prediction systems begin with labeled historical examples.
explain_back_prompt: Using the “The Label Is Not Always Truth” story, explain Supervised Learning without assuming the listener knows machine learning.
